text.title: Rails Patterns Examples
text.summary: Worked example: extracting PlaceOrderService from a 95-line controller action, with the canonical ServiceResult and a service body whose side effect fires only after commit.

example.context: Rails 7 app. `OrdersController#create` is 95 lines: it validates, creates the order, decrements inventory, charges the card, sends the confirmation email and renders — all in one method, covered only by a request spec.
example.walk: Step 1: name the action — `PlaceOrder` in the `Orders` context. Step 2: `app/services/orders/place_order_service.rb` with `initialize(params:, current_user:, gateway:, inventory:)`, collaborators defaulting to the real implementations. Step 3: `call` wraps the order creation, the inventory reservation and the charge in one `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction`, returns `ServiceResult.success(data: order)` on the happy path and `ServiceResult.failure(error: :insufficient_stock)` or `:payment_declined` on a business failure — never a raise. Step 4: the confirmation mail moves out of the transaction into an `after_create_commit` hook, so a rollback cannot email a customer about an order that does not exist. Step 5: the controller action becomes six lines branching on `result.success?`. Step 6: `spec/services/orders/place_order_service_spec.rb` covers twelve cases with mocked collaborators.
example.output: The controller action drops to 6 lines; the service is ~80 lines; the service specs run in ~200 ms against ~4 s for the equivalent request specs; every failure mode is a named symbol a caller can match on.

example.note: One class, four methods, no subclasses — `single-serviceresult`. A CI grep fails the build on a second `class ServiceResult`.

example.code:
module Orders class PlaceOrderService def initialize(params:, current_user:, gateway: PaymentGateway.instance, inventory: InventoryService.new) @params, @current_user, @gateway, @inventory = params, current_user, gateway, inventory end
def call order = nil
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do order = build_order return ServiceResult.failure(error: :invalid_params, details: order.errors) unless order.save return ServiceResult.failure(error: :insufficient_stock) unless @inventory.reserve(order.items).success?
charge = @gateway.charge(amount: order.total_cents, customer: @current_user) return ServiceResult.failure(error: :payment_declined) unless charge.success?
order.update!(charge_id: charge.id, status: :paid) end
ServiceResult.success(data: order) # mail fires from after_create_commit, not from here end
private
def build_order @current_user.orders.build(@params).tap do |order| order.status = :pending order.placed_at = Time.current end end end end
example.note: One action, `params:` / `current_user:` kwargs, the transaction owned by the service, failures as results rather than raises, and no `deliver_later` inside the transaction — `side-effects-after-commit`.
